messages.subject: Re: Error in intI
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gengping, sorry for the delay in response. This is an error I've seen before, and likely has to do with you trying to fit a highly complex model with lots of hinge features. Maxnet can't handle this well all the time, whereas maxent.jar sometimes can. Could you please give us specifics about what you tried to do that gave you the error? Which model did you run, what were the settings, etc.?

Jamie

messages.subject: Project to the past
messages.body_plain: Do you know how can I project a model that I get using Wallace, to the past, using layers that I already get?
messages.body_snippet: Do you know how can I project a model that I get using Wallace, to the past, using layers that I already get?

messages.subject: Project to the past
messages.body_plain: Run the analysis you want with all the settings you plan to use and do a projection to the future in the extent you want to project to the past. After you get your projection get the code as an R markdown. Go in and swap the future data with your past data. That's how I've been doing it at least.

messages.subject: Re: Project to the past
messages.body_plain:
Justin, thanks for providing a great answer. Alejandro, yes, that is the only way to make past projections in Wallace currently. If you need assistance with customizing the RMarkdown code, please ask.

The reason we can only offer future projections is because you cannot currently access the past climate layers in Worldclim through the raster package. We have been talking about writing some custom functions to pull the data off the Worldclim server, but have not implemented this yet. If code happens to arise that does this in the iterim, we'd love to include it to provide this functionality.
